result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make empathy more immediate and universal — not just feeling for others in distant, abstract moments, but truly understanding their experiences, fears, and hopes as clearly as our own.

Many of humanity’s deepest problems — cruelty, neglect, exploitation, polarization — are failures of empathy at scale. If people could genuinely feel the consequences of their actions on others, many systems would change naturally: how we treat the poor, the environment, animals, enemies, strangers, and even ourselves.

Empathy wouldn’t solve everything, but it would make it much harder to ignore suffering — and much easier to build cooperation, justice, and care into the structures of the world.
